image_description: A close-up photograph of a bicycle wheel hub featuring a mechanical disc brake system. The image shows a perforated metal rotor (disc) with a wavy outer edge, mounted to the center of a spoked wheel. A black caliper assembly is mounted to the white front fork of the bicycle, straddling the rotor. A black quick-release skewer lever is visible at the axle center. The background consists of blurred concrete ground.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Circular metal rotor (disc), notably larger in diameter than its thickness.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rotor is clearly circular and thin relative to its diameter, consistent with a bicycle disc brake.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Caliper is cast metal mounted over rotor edge.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A black mechanical caliper is visible mounted to the fork, positioned over the edge of the rotor.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rotor is mounted to wheel hub with visible lug bolt pattern.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: This checkpoint describes an automotive hub with lug bolts. The image shows a bicycle hub with a quick-release skewer and spokes; the mounting interface (6-bolt or Centerlock) is obscured by the skewer lever and angle.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rotor is ventilated (two plates with cooling fins) or solid.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rotor is a single solid plate with cutouts for weight reduction and cooling, which fits the 'solid' description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Brake pads are rectangular friction material blocks pressing against rotor faces.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The brake pads are internal to the caliper housing and are not directly visible from this external angle.
The caliper appears to be a mechanical (cable-actuated) type rather than hydraulic, as there is no visible hydraulic hose or banjo bolt fitting. A cable housing stop may be present but is indistinct.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Surface shows machined concentric grooves or cross-drilled holes.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rotor surface appears smooth without distinct machined grooves or cross-drilling patterns typical of high-performance automotive rotors. It features large structural cutouts instead.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Surface exhibits heat discoloration (blue/brown tint) from use.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rotor surface is uniform silver/grey metal color with no visible blueing or browning indicative of significant heat stress.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Caliper is cast aluminum or iron.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The caliper has the appearance of cast metal, likely aluminum alloy given the application.

artifact_observations.location: White sticker on the bicycle fork
artifact_observations.reasoning: There is a decal on the fork with a stylized logo/text. The characters are somewhat distorted and lack sharp definition, typical of AI struggling with small text, though it could also be low-resolution photography.
The geometry of the spokes behind the rotor cutouts appears slightly inconsistent. Some spokes seem to merge or fade into the background blur unnaturally, lacking clear occlusion boundaries.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the object is correctly classified as a disk brake and distinguish between automotive and bicycle variants.
To verify the structural integrity of the thin spokes and the complex cutouts of the rotor, checking for melting or fusion artifacts.
To ensure the caliper is correctly positioned in 3D space relative to the fork and rotor, checking for depth bleeding.
To analyze the legibility and structure of the text/logo on the fork sticker.
